contexts.text: The more (friendship and civility) derive from charity, the more sincere they are.
Unfermented = what is sincere; thus from a sincere heart...
Outwardly appears sincere and good.
(These Spirits) live together in such sincerity that they hide nothing... For acts with those in sincerity are in the conscience...
Man is (then) not in good, because not in what is sincere.
From the mere tone I could perceive whether they spoke from... what is sincere.
They were told that this is evil... because it is not sincere to speak so; for they who are sincere do not want to speak, or even think, anything but what others may know...
What is sincere and modest shone from them.
In the most ancient times there was sincerity. Described.
So long as there were sincerity and rectitude, such speech (by the face) remained...
The quality of a sincere and just man. Explained.
The poor who... act sincerely and faithfully.
Love what is sincere and right because it is sincere and right.
Man becomes rational to the second degree by the love of what is sincere and right.
One may act sincerely and justly with an associate that he may appear to be sincere and just... another, for the sake of the world and gain; (and so on). Explained.
Those also act sincerely and justly... who act from the love of what is sincere and just; some from obedience; some from the good of faith; (and so on). Explained.
Heavenly love is to love what is good, sincere, and just, because it is good, sincere, and just... Hence they have the life of what is good, sincere, and just, which is heavenly life.
What is sincere and right is of moral life; what is just and fair, of civil life.
They who have thought from the Divine nothing but what is sincere and just, have shining faces.
Man is accustomed from infancy to make a show of sincerity, etc.
Civil and moral good and truth, which are called just and sincere...
All (civil and moral) laws relate to what is sincere and right.
Who does not want to be called sincere?... Almost all exercise sincerity and justice in externals... as if they acted from real sincerity and justice.
Then, in doing what is sincere and just, which are of moral and civil life, he acts from a spiritual origin; (thus) from real sincerity and justice.
His justice and sincerity, in the external form, appear exactly like the justice and sincerity with natural men; but in the internal form they are entirely unlike. Explained.
(Such) laugh at sincerity and justice.
Consequently, what is sincere and just (is the neighbour); and therefore he who... acts sincerely and justly, for the sake of what is sincere and just, loves the neighbour...
That... moral good, which is the good of life in society, and is called what is sincere, is the neighbour. References.
(The English) love sincerity.
In proportion as anyone shuns thefts of every kind as sins, he loves sincerity. General article.
For fraud and sincerity are two opposites.
By sincerity are also meant integrity, justice, fidelity, and rectitude...
Unless one is interiorly sincere... he is insincere. Illustrated.
There are moral men who... exercise sincerity, etc., (and yet remain merely natural). Explained.
With spiritual and sincere men (these two respirations) are rarely separated.
(Such) speak more simply and sincerely than others.
a. [2]. The Internal and External make a one solely with those who are sincere at heart.
The virtues which pertain to the moral wisdom of males are sincerity, etc.
5. So far as anyone does not want to steal, he practises sincerity.
Who loves a merchant except for his sincerity?
Such speech has in it that it is not sincere; for they who are sincere want others to know everything they think...
Societies of friendship sufficiently sincere.
Have insinuated themselves under the guise of friendship and sincerity.
Such spoke sincerely; but they defile all sincere utterance, because the intention is unclean.
As they had sincerity hereditarily from ancient times... and have destroyed it... they are now among the worst in Sweden.
Like many others (the Swedes) can make a show of external sincerity... insomuch that in the other life they can deceive whoever they want by this external sincerity.
They could avert their minds by an influx of external sincerity.
Those who are sincere in externals, but evil in internals. They make a show of sincerity, and thereby persuade the simple.
Their speech was sincere, but within they were devils.
The reason (the English have an interior sight as regards religion) is that they act sincerely among themselves, without deceit...
They love what is sincere, and act from what is sincere; and this is general with them.
A multitude whose speech sounded sincere... In the world they had affected a reputation for sincerity; but within were devoid of conscience.

(The heavenly doctrine) is not difficult, for it only wants us to live sincerely, in our calling and out of it, with every person and in every thing; because if otherwise, it is sin... They said they want to live sincerely; but when examined, it was found they did not, for they want to use fraud, cunning, and deceit... and to injure others in many other ways... They were therefore sent away; for to live sincerely includes all such things. Enumerated... No one can live sincerely for the sake of God and the neighbour, but he who is Christian as to the life.
(These) speak sincerely... and make a show not so much of sanctity as of sincerity. Described.
(The English nation) are kept in what is sincere and just by their not being allowed to cheat, rob, and kill.
Two things are requisite... SE 2. That one lives sincere, so that one shuns external evils...
On those who by mere sincere speech can persuade the simple...
Newton is a very sincere man.
One who outwardly appeared sincere, but was a devil within.
Exercise sincerity and justice, but for the sake of reputation, etc.
For sincerity is moral good and truth, and justice is civil good and truth. AE 831:5.
They had loved sincerity... because they had reputed frauds as nefarious.
After some short combats (against stealing) they are led by the Lord into the good called sincerity...
If they are persuaded that he is a learned and sincere man.
Appear sincere for the sake of gain.
They are sincere in externals; but insincere in internals.
